PullRequest.Title: chat: Warn about BYOK models in remote Copilot sessions

## Summary

BYOK models are not supported by the Copilot harness in remote sessions. Add a chat-input warning in the editor so users with configured BYOK models understand this limitation.

- Require an actual resolved BYOK model, the Copilot harness, and a live connection to the selected remote host or remote workspace.
- Never show the warning in the Agents window, for local sessions, or for other harnesses.
- Limit the warning to the first eligible input/session per editor-window instance. Model changes and reconnections do not reset dismissal.
- Wait for a concrete session resource before displaying the warning so startup does not prematurely consume the one-time notice.
- Offer **Don't Show Again**, persisted per profile across reloads.
- Pass the rendering input context to the existing notification `onDidShow` callback to enforce first-input ownership.
- Update accessibility help and add regression coverage for connection state, startup, message sending, and profile-isolated muting.

No linked issue was provided.

## Testing

Passed:
- `npm run compile-client` — completed with 0 errors.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostRemoteByokNotification.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/widget/input/chatInputNotificationWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/accessibility/chatAccessibilityHelp.test.ts` — 110 tests passed.
- `node build/hygiene.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostRemoteByokNotification.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostRemoteByokNotification.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --cached --check` and the normal pre-commit hygiene hook — passed.

Manual verification in the OSS editor using TestResolver and a synthetic BYOK provider registered through the real language-model service:
- A connected remote Copilot input displays the warning when the provider resolves.
- Keyboard dismissal restores focus to the chat input.
- Starting another chat and re-registering the provider do not repeat the warning.
- After ordinary dismissal, **Developer: Reload Window** allows the warning to appear again once the session initializes.
- **Don't Show Again** hides the warning and persists through new chats, provider changes, and **Developer: Reload Window**.

For manual verification in a fresh, unmuted OSS editor profile, use the built-in TestResolver (`./scripts/code.sh --remote=test+test`); Remote-SSH does not support OSS:
1. Connect the remote workspace and select the Agent Host Copilot harness.
2. With no BYOK models, confirm no warning. Add the first BYOK model and wait for discovery; the warning should appear without reloading.
3. Confirm local sessions, other harnesses, disconnected hosts, and the Agents window do not show it.
4. Confirm other chat inputs/sessions do not repeat the warning in the same window.
5. Select **Don't Show Again**, reload the window, and confirm it stays hidden.

Not fully verified manually: real provider authentication, SSH/WSL/Dev Container/Codespaces transports, actual network interruption, multiple concurrent windows, full application restart, physical screen-reader output, and the complete theme/layout matrix. Automated connection-state and widget tests do not substitute for those environment-specific checks.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed listener, reconnect event sequence, three-hour retry lifetime, synchronous global event fan-out, and widget DOM rebuild are all directly traced in repository code. The exact duration of each rebuild depends on the number and complexity of open chat inputs, affecting severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: main-thread DOM teardown/recreation, notification predicate work, and associated object allocations in every mounted ChatInputNotificationWidget
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost is O(reconnect state events × mounted chat inputs × registered notifications). The reconnect loop emits ConnectionLost plus ReconnectionWait and ReconnectionRunning on every attempt; after its initial schedule it can retry every 30 seconds for the three-hour grace period, while each event reaches every mounted chat input.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: repeated main-thread rendering and allocation/GC pressure, causing intermittent UI stalls during prolonged remote outages
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Remote connection state changes did not refresh the global chat-input notification service, so reconnect attempts did not rebuild notification DOM in every chat input.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added unfiltered onDidStateChange listener calls _refresh for ConnectionLost, every ReconnectionWait, every ReconnectionRunning, ConnectionGain, and permanent failure. _refresh synchronously fires the notification service's global onDidChange event, whose listeners clear and rebuild each ChatInputNotificationWidget.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line `this._register(remoteConnection.onDidStateChange(() => this._refresh()));` newly maps every remote transport state event to a global synchronous notification refresh.
Findings.Title: Coalesce reconnect states before refreshing every chat input
Findings.Impact: In any remote workspace, including users with no BYOK models and no eligible Copilot session, a prolonged network outage repeatedly tears down and recreates active notification UI across all open chat inputs on every reconnect phase. This can produce recurring main-thread jank while the editor is already handling a degraded connection.
Findings.Evidence: PersistentConnection._runReconnectingLoop emits ConnectionLost once and then ReconnectionWait/ReconnectionRunning for each retry, eventually using a 30-second interval under ProtocolConstants.ReconnectionGraceTime (3 hours). ChatInputNotificationService.refresh synchronously fires onDidChange, and each ChatInputNotificationWidget listener calls _render(), which clears its DOM/disposables and reconstructs the selected notification. BYOK eligibility only observes connection.isConnected, so intermediate wait/running events after the first loss cannot change the predicate.
Findings.Recommendation: Track the previous `isConnected` value and refresh only when that boolean changes (for example, map state events to `remoteConnection.isConnected` and latch duplicates). Once the one-time notice has been dismissed because its claimed connection became ineligible, stop refreshing for later reconnect phases; also avoid the extra unconditional refresh when dismissNotification already emitted a change.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remote workspace management connection startup and late connection-state subscribers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing lazy remote management handshake must complete before remote channels progress. The diff only stores the latest transport state and exposes a synchronous getter; forwarding the synthetic initial ConnectionGain occurs after the client is connected and is not awaited by connection creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Establish the remote management transport and IPC client
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lazy initial connection per remote editor window; reconnections reuse the persistent connection flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same remote management connection and reconnect operations occurred without a current-state getter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for remote channels, but pre-existing; the new state bookkeeping adds no network operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Propagate extensionHostEnv to extension-host managers from a ConnectionGain listener when that Eventually-phase contribution is already attached
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per extension-host manager for the newly forwarded initial gain, plus the pre-existing calls after actual reconnections; only when extensionHostEnv exists and startup ordering leaves the listener attached first.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The wrapper did not forward PersistentConnection's constructor-time initial gain, so this listener normally handled reconnection gains only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Async listener work is not awaited by connection creation, so it is off the management-connection critical path. Resolver work is cache-coalesced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit remoteConnectionGain telemetry through the telemetry service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional telemetry event for the newly forwarded initial gain when the listener is attached before lazy connection establishment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only later reconnection gains reached the wrapper listener.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Telemetry logging is off the connection critical path and bounded to one event.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One management connection per remote editor window and the number of state-event subscribers/extension-host managers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The management connection remains a single serialized connection. Event listeners run synchronously; async listener work is started without being awaited by the emitter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The authority resolver coalesces and caches one DeferredPromise per authority, so a ConnectionGain listener's resolveAuthority call reuses the resolved result. The new state getter is an in-memory scalar with no cache miss path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that state reads are local and the synthetic event is forwarded after connection establishment; medium confidence on which Eventually-phase listeners are attached first in every product startup ordering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Lazy connection and contribution startup ordering determines which existing listeners observe the synthetic initial gain, but all newly reached work is bounded and off the handshake critical path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable startup regression: the possible added event fan-out is bounded, cached where relevant, and off the critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remote workspace network outage while chat inputs are mounted
Scenarios.CriticalPath: PersistentConnection synchronously emits each reconnect state on the renderer thread. The new listener immediately calls the global notification service refresh, whose synchronous listeners clear and rebuild each mounted chat notification widget before reconnect processing continues to its next async boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reconnect the existing remote management transport
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized network attempt per retry; wait/running state pairs continue at up to one attempt per 30 seconds for the three-hour grace window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same serialized reconnect attempts occurred without globally refreshing chat input notifications for every intermediate state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The network reconnect is pre-existing. The new synchronous render fan-out runs immediately before each attempt/wait progression and consumes renderer main-thread time.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Reconnect state count multiplied by mounted ChatInputPart instances and registered/active notifications. The three-hour grace period can produce repeated wait/running pairs every 30 seconds after the initial retry schedule.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Reconnect attempts are serialized, but every state event synchronously fans out to all mounted widgets; there is no state deduplication, coalescing, or render batching.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Connection liveness is cached as one enum, but the listener ignores whether isConnected actually changed. Notification predicates re-read local model/storage/connection state on every refresh; no render-result cache prevents DOM reconstruction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the unfiltered added listener, reconnect sequence, synchronous service emitter, and full widget DOM rebuild are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact stall depends on how many chat editors and how complex their currently selected notifications are, but all remote workspaces can hit the mechanism even with no BYOK model.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable performance regression: intermediate reconnect states that cannot change boolean eligibility repeatedly rebuild notification DOM across all chat inputs.

Scenarios.Scenario: BYOK warning discovery, display, dismissal, and model/agent-host changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After restoration, the contribution registers one notification. Model, entitlement, agent-host connection, profile-storage, and workspace-connection events synchronously refresh mounted inputs; rendering scans local model metadata and connection arrays. Showing the warning performs one nested global refresh to claim the first input.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the profile-scoped Don't Show Again preference
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One profile storage write per explicit user activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No BYOK-warning preference existed, so this write did not occur.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The command issues the write synchronously through the storage service, but it is user-triggered, constant-cardinality, and not part of ordinary rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of model-change events, mounted chat inputs, registered notifications, language-model IDs, and remote agent-host connection records. After first display, non-owner contexts reject before scanning models.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All refresh and render work is synchronous on the UI thread. Events are not coalesced. The first-visible claim adds one bounded nested refresh.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Language model IDs are copied from an in-memory Map and lookups are Map reads; vendor resolution and remote-host connection status are cached service state. The contribution does not cache whether any eligible BYOK model exists, but model events are per changed vendor/configuration rather than per render frame.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in local-only eligibility checks and synchronous render fan-out.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installed model/vendor count and simultaneous chat editor count vary, but local Map/array scans are generally modest. The reconnect-specific unbounded repetition is handled in the separate reported scenario.
Scenarios.Verdict: Aside from the separately reported reconnect fan-out, discovery and one-time display work is bounded and does not establish another high-confidence performance issue.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Accessibility help text is assembled synchronously when requested; the diff adds one conditional localized string before the help UI can display.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fixed string for each explicit help invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous text assembly with no queue or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changed cache behavior; localization lookup follows the existing help-text pattern.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the added work is constant-size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; constant-time local string insertion only.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 15 changed files and traced remote startup/reconnect events, global chat notification rendering, model/connection eligibility checks, profile storage, and accessibility help. Submitted one medium synchronous-rendering finding for uncoalesced reconnect-state fan-out; no concrete regression fix requiring blame was present.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
